The testbed was created and tested using the AutoSched AP simulation software. The interface for 
Autosched AP is a set of Excel sheets. Users can either use the model directly in Autosched AP or 
transfer the data from the E xcel data sheets to the simulation tool of their choice. The main features 
of the two data sets are described in Sections 2 and 3 in an almost dataset -independent manner, 
whereas the main differences between specific datasets are summarized in Section 4. 
An AutoSched AP simulation model is located in the folder model_name.asd. It consists of several files 
with extension .txt. To create or change a model, the Excel software can be used. The Excel sheets and 
the corresponding tables will be transformed into the model files (.txt) by exporting the model. 
2. Minimal Structure 
The minimal structure of the models consists of the products, the tools, and the basic data connecting 
between them (processing time, release rate in the fab, etc.). This minimal structure is fully contained 
in the five files necessary to run the simulation models in AutoSched AP. These files are described in 
the following subsections. 
2.1. options.def 
This master file is used to control the simulation model. Here, all files and options are listed, for 
instance, the start date of the simulation , see SIM_START (line 1) in Fi gure 1. The file names are 
assigned to the type of the file, e.g. part.txt is a PRODUCT_FILES file (line 12). Furthermore, files can 
be activated or deactivated, e.g. additional order files to include engineering lots can be used or not. 
STATION_FILES are the files describing the machines (tools). In our case, the file is called tool.txt (see 
Section 2.2 for a more detailed description of the file tool.txt). 
2.2. tool.txt 
 
This file describes the machines, called tools, their quantity, and the related rules for lot dispatching. 
Station families (tool groups) are declared by theirs names in the column STNFAM and the number of 
tools in the column STNQTY (the default value is one if there is no number defined). All tools of a tool 
group are assumed to be identical. The name of the first tool (station) is defined in the column STN. 
Moreover, the tool groups (station families) ar

2.3. part.txt 
In this file (see Figure 3), the different products are declared by name (PART) and their route (ROUTE). 
The names are used for providing lot release information in the order.txt file, see Figure 5. In addition, 
the file name of the route is required (ROUTEFILE). The columns PARTGRP and PARTFAM can be used 
to group related products (PART), e.g. for specific batching criteria. Further, these columns allow for

2.4. route_i.txt 
Overall, ten routes (products) are defined in the testbed. All the ten routes are used in dataset 2, while 
only the products 3 and 4 are included in dataset 1. The details of the required set of process steps are 
found in the set of files denoted as route_i.txt, i = 1,…,10. It is also possible to use only a single file that 
contains all routes. 
Each route consists of multiple process steps, e.g. 583 process steps exist for part_3. Each step requires 
the name of the route (ROUTE), the name of the step (STEP; here an integer ), the used tool group 
(STNFAM), and the processing time. The latter will be defined by a probability distribution (PDIST), the 
amount of time (PTIME a nd PTIME2), the time units (PUNITS; here in minutes), and the entity type 
(PTPER) (cf. Figure 4). Hence, the time can be applied for each single wafer (per_piece), for a lot 
(per_lot), or for a batch (per_batch) in which case the number of wafers in the ba tch are determined 
by a minimum and maximum batch size (BATCHMIN and BATCHMAX). Note that a continuous uniform 
distribution is used (PDIST) which requires two parameters (PTIME, PTIME2). PTIME is the mean, while 
PTIME2 represents the offset. 
Important: The processing sequence is independent from step names (integer values), but it depends 
on the order from the top to the bottom. The process step is described in the column DESC, here by 
the original name of the process step. It is provided for the user, but does not affect the simulation. 
The remaining columns will be explained when the corresponding additional features are described.

Lots have to be released into the simulation model. Therefore, the name of the lot (LOT), the name of

To repeat the release of lots after a fixed amount of time, the length of the interval (REPEAT, RUNITS) 
and the number of replications (RPT#) have to be specified. The number of lots released per interval is 
defined in the column LOTSPERRPT (the default value is again 1). Furthermore, for each product at 
least one interval is defined, while a constant distribution is used (RDIST). It is also possible to assign 
more than one order to a product, for instance for regular lots and hot lots (cf. Figure 5 lines 2 and 4). 
There are priorities for the different lot types, they ar e used for lot ranking (PRIOR). A higher priority 
value indicates a higher importance of a lot. Note that the lot names starting from the second lot will

3.1.1. Unscheduled Down Times: Breakdowns 
Used files: downcal.txt, attach.txt 
Breakdowns are described in downcal.txt, i.e. different down scenarios with their probability 
distributions of the corresponding Time To Failure (TTF) and Time To Repair (TTR) values are collected 
(see Figure 7). 
For every station group (area) a down scenario is defined which can be identified by i ts name 
(DOWNCALNAME). Breakdowns are triggered based on calendars (mttf_by_cal in column 
DOWNCALTYPE), and the tool usage has no impact on their occurrence. Each breakdo wn type is 
characterized by the probability distributions of its TTF and TTR values. T he distribution type is given 
(MTTFDIST and MTTRDIST, here both exponential ly distributed ). The mean of TTR and TTF (MTTF, 
MTTR) and their time units are needed (MTTFUNITS and MTTRUNITS, here in minutes).

the distribution type is stated (here exponentially distributed). The mean of the first TTF (FOA) and the

3.1.2. Scheduled Down Times: Preventive Maintenance (PM) 
Used files: pmcal.txt, attach.txt 
The representation of PMs works almost in the same way as for breakdowns (cf. Figure 8). Here, two 
types for the Mean Time Between PM (MTBPM) values are distinguished (PMCALTYPE). The PM is time-
based for diffusion, lithography, and metrology represented by mtbm_by_cal to consider the calendar 
time. For all other tool groups, the PM is counter-based by applying mtbpm_by_pieces, i.e., a PM must 
be executed after processing a prescribed numb er of wafers. Hence, the corresponding numbers and 
units are needed in the columns MTBPM and MTBPMUNITS. Note that no special probability 
distribution is defined for MTBPM (the default is constant). However, the time -based PMs are 
practically launched as Mean Time Before PM, so that the PM duration itself is included in the MTBPM 
value. 
A continuous uniform distribution is used to represent the TTR value that requires values for the two 
parameters MTTR and MTTR2 (mean and offset) and the time unit (MTTRUNITS). For instance, each

DefMet_BE_33 in the lines 2 and 3. In attach.txt file, line 13, a monthly PM is allocated to the station 
family (RESTYPE = stnfam). Moreover, counter-based PMs are also applied for each station family, i.e., 
the used RESTYPE is stnfam and the RESNAME is the name of the tool group (see file “attach.txt” or 
Figure 6, line 92). The prescribed number of wafers is valid for each individual tool of the tool group. 
The distribution of the first PM for the tools of a tool group is defined in the column FOADIST (see file 
“attach.txt”). The constant distribution means that the first PM for the tools of a tool set is evenly 
distributed based on the value in the column FOA. For example, a FOA value of 80 days with four tools 
lead to PMs for to ol 1, 2, 3, and 4 at the following days: 20, 40, 60, and 80. For counter -based PMs it

the continuous uniform distribution U(5, 10). For this purpose, a location is defined for each tool group 
in the column S TNFAMLOC (see tool.txt or Figure 10). An identical tool group location called Fab is 
used. The times from a specific location (FROMLOC) t o another (TOLOC) have to be specified in the 
fromto.txt file (see Figure 9). In the datasets, we use only from Fab to Fab as described before. The 
duration follows a continuous uniform distribution (DDIST) with the given parameter values (DTIME,

Used files: tool.txt, CustomActl.txt

and unload times are the same for all tool groups, their duration is 1 minute each (LTIME, LTUNITS for

the processing time. At first, a lot is loaded, processing then occurs, and finally, the lot is unloaded. To 
implement this behavior, it is nece ssary to use an appropriate action list (CustomActl.txt, Figure 14). 
Moreover, this is valid for each process step or each tool. Therefore, it is sufficient to define the used

3.5. Batching 
Used files: tool.txt, route_i.txt files 
Diffusion tools are able to process several lots at the same time on the same tool . We refer to the 
resulting group of jobs as a batch. Both the minimum possible batch size (BATCHMN) and the maximum 
possible batch size (BATCHMX) are defined at the relevant steps in the route files, e.g. in route_3.txt, 
lines 2 and 6 (see Figure 4). The sizes are given in number of wafers. Hence, in the column BATCHPER 
of tool.txt file piece has to be entered for each batch processing tool group, e.g. in line 119. Note that 
only lots of the same product at the same process step can be used to form a batch. For this purpose, 
the crit_sameroutestep batch criterion (BATCHCRITF) is used. 
It i s also possible t o allow batches with production lots belonging to a particular product and 
engineering lots from a specific engineering product derived from the former product. First, the same 
PARTFAM, e.g. “product_3”, has to be defined for the production product and the corresponding 
engineering product (see Figure 3). Moreover, two batch criteria crit_samepartfam and 
crit_samestepname has to be used, so that only lots with the same name of PARTFAM and at the same 
process step, i.e. the same name of the step, can be used to build a batch. 
3.6. Cascading 
Used files: options.def, tool.txt, route_i.txt files 
Cascading is a characteristic of some stations that are composed of a series of modules able to process 
materials simultaneously. Wafers/lots need to be processed by several modules one after the other, 
but while an earlier lot/wafer is undergoing a later phase in the process, the following lot/wafer can 
be undergoing an earlier phase in the process. As a result, the time required for the first wafer (or lot) 
to exit the machine is different (longer) than the time between successive lots. 
In order to model this, the semiconductor extension is applied. It is necessary to distinguish between 
cascading lots or wafers, i.e. whether the processing on a tool is per wafer or per lot. In any case, a 
station capacity (STNCAP) of 2 has to be stated in the tool.txt file, see lines 89 and 95 for each 
corresponding tool group . If there is no entry, e.g. line 92, no cascading is implemented since the 
default is 1. The processing times of the process steps are set in the route_i.txt file

In both models, a baseline rule is used to prioritize between lots queueing in front of any tool group. 
The First-Come First-Served (FCFS) dispatching rule is applied in dataset 1 representing a fab owned by 
a semiconductor company that produces to stock. For dataset 2 representing a foundry, i.e. it produces 
to order a large variety of products, the Critical Ratio (CR) dispatching rule is applied . Local rules and 
special lots that break the baseline rule are described in the following subsections. 
 
3.11. Hot Lots and Setup Avoidance 
Here, the rule_FIRST rule (RULE) and multiple ranking functions (FWLRANK) are used. They are defined 
for each tool group. At first, highest pr iority lots are preferred, i.e. hot lots before regular lots 
(rank_HP). This is stated in the PRIOR column in the order.txt file (Figure 5). Ranking is then carried out 
based on the least setup time (rank_RSETUP) and finally the FIFO (rank_FIFO) criteria. If there is one 
hot lot chosen, it can trigger a setup. If there are two or more hot l ots (same priority), they will be
